metadata.title: Understanding the relationship between teacher collaboration and instructional clarity via teacher self-efficacy: A moderated mediation model of organizational commitment

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses nationally representative U.S. TALIS 2018 data from lower secondary schools (grades 7–9), with teachers nested within schools. Sampling followed TALIS’s stratified two-stage cluster design (schools selected with probability proportional to size; teachers randomly selected within schools), and the authors apply TALIS 2018 teacher-level and school-level weights (tchwgt and schwgt) in multilevel modeling to account for unequal selection probabilities and nonresponse. The analytic sample is restricted to teachers who did not exclusively/primarily teach special needs students and to schools with at least three teachers, and missingness is handled via FIML rather than listwise deletion. Because the analysis is conducted with multilevel latent moderated structural equation modeling (Mplus) rather than ML algorithms, the paper does not discuss any ML-specific omission of weights; instead it explicitly states that weights are used at the corresponding levels.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The study does not use cognitive achievement Plausible Values (PV) because the dependent variables are teacher-reported latent constructs (teacher collaboration, clarity of instruction, teacher self-efficacy, and organizational commitment) rather than PV-based achievement scores. For missing data, the authors report using Full Information Maximum Likelihood Estimation (FIML) to address missingness, which is treated here as a multiple-imputation-like approach per the provided mapping rules. The paper provides the missingness proportion range and reports Little’s MCAR test results, supporting that the missing-data strategy is documented rather than omitted.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used TALIS 2018 nationally representative U.S. lower secondary school data (grades 7–9). The initial teacher survey sample included 2560 teachers in 165 schools; teachers who exclusively or primarily taught special needs students in the target class were removed. The analytic sample was restricted to 2004 teachers in 165 schools, then further excluded schools with fewer than three teachers to reduce bias in the multilevel structure. Missing data were handled using FIML, and the final analytic sample comprised 1897 teachers across 156 schools.

main_findings.dataset_used: TALIS 2018 (U.S., lower secondary grades 7–9) — teacher-level multilevel latent moderated mediation
main_findings.performance_metrics: MSEM (1-1-1 multilevel): Direct effect of teacher collaboration on clarity β=0.156 (p<0.001, 95% CI [0.090, 0.222]); Indirect effect via teacher self-efficacy β=0.148 (p<0.001, 95% CI [0.106, 0.190]); Total effect β=0.304 (p<0.001, 95% CI [0.230, 0.378]). Moderated mediation (conditional indirect B): +1 SD OC B=0.119 (p<0.01, 95% LLCI 0.055, 95% ULCI 0.184); Mean OC B=0.092 (p<0.01, 95% LLCI 0.041, 95% ULCI 0.143); −1 SD OC B=0.064 (p<0.05, 95% LLCI 0.019, 95% ULCI 0.109).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TALIS 2018 (U.S., lower secondary grades 7–9) the study leveraged teacher collaboration, teacher self-efficacy in instruction, and organizational commitment to model clarity of instruction, finding that teacher collaboration had a positive direct effect on clarity (β=0.156) and an additional positive indirect effect through teacher self-efficacy (β=0.148), with a positive total effect (β=0.304). This indicates that strengthening teacher collaboration—especially in schools where teachers show higher organizational commitment—may improve instructional clarity, though the cross-sectional design limits causal interpretation.

data.outcome_summary: This study analyzes nationally representative U.S. TALIS 2018 data from lower secondary schools (grades 7–9), using a multilevel latent moderated structural equation modeling framework with teachers nested within schools. The analytic sample includes 1,897 teachers across 156 schools after excluding teachers who exclusively/primarily taught special needs students and removing schools with fewer than three teachers; missingness (up to ~4%) is handled using FIML. The results show that teacher collaboration is positively associated with clarity of instruction both directly (β=0.156, p<0.001) and indirectly via teacher self-efficacy in instruction (β=0.148, p<0.001), yielding a total standardized effect of β=0.304 (p<0.001). Organizational commitment moderates the mediated pathway, with stronger conditional indirect effects at higher commitment (+1 SD OC B=0.119) than at lower commitment (−1 SD OC B=0.064). Because the study relies on teacher self-reports and cross-sectional data, findings should not be interpreted as causal.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is sparse with respect to ML because the paper does not train predictive machine-learning models; instead it uses multilevel latent moderated structural equation modeling (MSEM) with latent constructs and bootstrapped confidence intervals for moderated mediation. As a result, the ML technique fields are intentionally left empty (no supervised ML algorithms are evaluated), while the substantive results are reported as structural path coefficients and mediation/moderation effects.
